## Descriptive statistics


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
summary(p$age_of_participants)
```

```

  18.00   29.00   42.00   43.85   58.00   95.00 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
sd(p$age_of_participants)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 17.36487
```


:::
:::


### Frequency tables


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
freq_table <- table(p$past_history_of_diabetes)
prop_table <- prop.table(freq_table)
combined_table <- data.frame(
  Frequency = freq_table,
  Percentage = prop_table * 100
)
combined_table
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  Frequency.Var1 Frequency.Freq Percentage.Var1 Percentage.Freq
1             no            597              no       94.611727
2            yes             34             yes        5.388273
```


:::
:::


### Grouped summaries


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
summary_table <- p %>%
  mutate(wealth_index = factor(wealth_index_of_participants)) %>% 
  group_by(wealth_index) %>%
  reframe(
    Frequency = n(),
    Percentage = paste0(round(n() * 100 / nrow(p), 2), "%")
  )
summary_table
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}


## Hypothesis testing

### Chi-square goodness-of-fit


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
observed <- table(p$ever_screened_for_bp)
expected <- c(1/2, 1/2) * sum(observed)
chisq_test <- chisq.test(x = observed, p = expected / sum(observed))
chisq_test
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Chi-squared test for given probabilities

data:  observed
X-squared = 80.23, df = 1, p-value < 2.2e-16
```


:::
:::


### Chi-square test for association


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
table_gender_dm <- table(p$sex_of_participants, p$past_history_of_diabetes)
chisq_m_5_b <- chisq.test(table_gender_dm, correct = FALSE)
chisq_m_5_b
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Pearson's Chi-squared test

data:  table_gender_dm
X-squared = 0.40978, df = 1, p-value = 0.5221
```


:::
:::


### McNemar test for paired binary responses


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
table_bfr_aftr <- table(p$pain_foot_bfr, p$pain_foot_aftr)
mcnemar_test <- mcnemar.test(table_bfr_aftr)
mcnemar_test
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	McNemar's Chi-squared test with continuity correction

data:  table_bfr_aftr
McNemar's chi-squared = 0.20712, df = 1, p-value = 0.649
```


:::
:::

These examples show the R workflow for medical data: import, clean, summarize, test, and visualize.

## Automating Analysis with Loops

Real datasets often need the same test or summary repeated across many variables. Loops (and their `apply`/`purrr` equivalents) let you do that without copy-pasting code.

### `for` loops


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
vars <- c("age_of_participants", "sbp_in_mm_hg", "dbp_in_mm_hg")

for (v in vars) {
  cat("Summary of", v, ":\n")
  print(summary(p[[v]]))
  cat("\n")
}
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Summary of age_of_participants :
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
  18.00   29.00   42.00   43.85   58.00   95.00 

Summary of sbp_in_mm_hg :
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
   83.0   108.0   120.0   120.8   130.5   199.0 

Summary of dbp_in_mm_hg :
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
  52.00   86.00  108.00   97.31  108.00  125.00 
```


:::
:::


### A shorter alternative: `sapply()`

For simple per-column operations the `apply` family avoids manual bookkeeping:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Same variables as the for-loop above, without the explicit loop
sapply(p[vars], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
age_of_participants        sbp_in_mm_hg        dbp_in_mm_hg 
           43.84786           120.75911            97.30586 
```


:::
:::


Use a `for` loop when each iteration has side effects (printing, saving files, building up a report) or when the logic is easier to follow step-by-step; reach for `sapply()` when you just need one result per element.

:::

::: {when-level="advanced"}

### `while` loops


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Halve a sample size threshold until it drops below 10
n <- nrow(p)
threshold <- n

while (threshold > 10) {
  threshold <- threshold %/% 2
}

cat("Final threshold:", threshold, "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Final threshold: 9 
```


:::
:::


### `repeat` loops


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# repeat runs until an explicit break condition is met
count <- 0
repeat {
  count <- count + 1
  if (count >= 5) break
}
count
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 5
```


:::
:::


### Tidy iteration with `purrr::map()`

`purrr::map()` and its typed variants return exactly the type you ask for, which makes them safer than `sapply()` inside larger pipelines:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(purrr)

map_dbl(p[vars], ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
age_of_participants        sbp_in_mm_hg        dbp_in_mm_hg 
           17.36487            16.80124            14.04460 
```


:::
:::
